- Expect opponents' Baubles: Affinity runs one in 67.7% of sideboards, Energy in 26.3%.

- Kappa Cannoneer has ward {4} and can't be blocked on turns an artifact enters. Pinnacle Emissary makes flying Drones. You have to race them.

# Golgari Soultrader Aristocrats (Modern, brew)

## The plan
Get three creatures out: Warren Soultrader, Gravecrawler, and a drain creature (Marionette Apprentice or Zulaport Cutthroat). Each loop goes like this: pay 1 life and sacrifice Gravecrawler to Soultrader to make a Treasure. Then use the Treasure to recast Gravecrawler from your graveyard. Soultrader is a Zombie, which is what lets you do that. With Apprentice out, the opponent loses 1 life when Gravecrawler dies and 1 more when the Treasure is used up. That's 2 per loop, and you can repeat it as often as you like. Fiend Artisan and Eldritch Evolution can put a missing piece straight onto the battlefield, so you usually only need two pieces plus a tutor.

## Why the key cards
- **Eldritch Evolution**: sacrificing Gravecrawler (mana value 1) lets it fetch a creature with mana value 3 or less, which includes Soultrader. Gravecrawler then waits in the graveyard to be recast. This is the fastest line.
- **Fiend Artisan**: a second tutor. Getting Soultrader costs {3} plus {B/G}, a creature to sacrifice, and sorcery timing. So it's a turn-4 play.
- **Zulaport Cutthroat**: each loop drains 1 and gains you 1, so it makes up for the life you pay to Soultrader.
- **Malevolent Rumble**: digs 4 cards deep for a piece and makes an Eldrazi Spawn you can sacrifice.
- **Interaction**: Abrupt Decay, Fatal Push, Flare of Malice (free if you sacrifice Gravecrawler, which you can recast), Orcish Bowmasters and Thoughtseize.

## The one change: Thoughtseize down to 1 main, Orcish Bowmasters up to 3
- The two most-played decks right now are Broodscale Combo (14.9% of the field) and Prowess (10.7%).
- Prowess is low-curve aggro, and Thoughtseize's 2 life hurts there. Bowmasters picks off small creatures and Eldrazi Spawn.
- Bowmasters is also a creature, and its Orc Army token is one too. Both can be sacrificed to the combo or the tutors. Thoughtseize can't.
- The other two Thoughtseize are now in the sideboard (three there in total). Bowmasters copies across main and sideboard stay at 4, and Thoughtseize stays at 4.

## Mana (21 lands, 5,000 simulated games)
| | This deck | Real Soultrader Combo list |
|---|---|---|
| Mulligan rate | 8.7% | 8.5% |
| Hit all 4 land drops by turn 4 | 48.5% | 39.9% |
| Mana screw rate | 21.8% | 28.6% |
| Right colors, turns 1–6 | 89.9–94.7% | 82–88% |

- The deck has 14 green sources and 17 black. Every fetch land can find Overgrown Tomb.
- **Odds of drawing the combo naturally by turn 4:** 29.8% have all three pieces in hand, and 23.5% can cast them. That counts only drawn pieces, not anything found by Artisan, Evolution or Rumble. Your real chance of assembling it is higher, but I haven't measured by how much.

## Sideboarding against the field
- **Broodscale Combo (14.9%)**
  - In: 2 Haywire Mite, 2 Chomping Changeling, 1 Orcish Bowmasters.
  - Out: 3 Flare of Malice, 1 Thoughtseize, 1 Undead Butler.
  - 92.4% of their lists have Grafdigger's Cage in the sideboard. Cage stops you recasting Gravecrawler and stops your tutors putting creatures onto the battlefield. Mite and Changeling remove it, and they also handle Blade of the Bloodchief.
- **Prowess (10.7%)**
  - In: 1 Bowmasters, 1 Fatal Push, and possibly 2 Culling Ritual (it wipes most of their board, but also yours).
  - Out: 1 Thoughtseize, 2 Undead Butler, and Eldritch Evolutions if you bring in Ritual.
  - Lightning Bolt is in 99.9% of their lists, and it kills Soultrader. In my judgment, wait to cast Soultrader until you can start the loop that same turn.
  - Their sideboard has Consign to Memory (95.7%), Tormod's Crypt (49.6%) and Surgical Extraction (48.5%).
- **Blink (6.7%)**
  - In: 3 Thoughtseize.
  - Out: 2 Fatal Push, 1 Flare.
  - They run Fatal Push (76.7%) and Solitude (99.8%), so strip their hand first. Keep Abrupt Decay for Teferi, Time Raveler.
  - In my judgment this is one of your worst matchups.
- **Goryo's Vengeance, Living End, Storm**
  - In: 3 Thoughtseize, 2 Surgical Extraction, 2 Endurance (point it at their graveyard).
  - Out: Fatal Push, Flare, and 1–2 Bowmasters.
- **Affinity, Eldrazi Tron, Amulet Titan**
  - In: Haywire Mite and Chomping Changeling.
  - Abrupt Decay already does a lot of work here.
- **Graveyard hate (Rest in Peace, Grafdigger's Cage, Tormod's Crypt)**
  - Chomping Changeling destroys these.
  - It also counts as a Zombie, so Gravecrawler can be recast off it.

## Label and source
This is a **brew**. It borrows its mana and sideboard shape from the Soultrader Combo archetype (15 recent lists). The real lists are mono-black-based with Chthonian Nightmare and Phyrexian Tower. The green tutor package (Artisan, Evolution, Rumble, Decay) is new and hasn't been tested in tournaments.

## Not verified
- I worked out the loop from the card text. I haven't tested it in play.
- The matchup assessments are my judgment, not measured.
- No tool measured turn-3 kill rates or win rates.

# Dimir Mystic-Monarch (Pauper brew)

**The plan:** This is a Dimir (blue-black) draw-go deck. Cheap card-filtering spells and instant-speed answers keep you alive until turn 4–5. Then Thorn of the Black Rose makes you the monarch (you draw an extra card each turn until someone hits you), and Murmuring Mystic makes a 1/1 flying Bird token every time you cast an instant or sorcery. The birds block to protect the crown, the crown draws more spells, and more spells make more birds. Once the board is locked, you attack in the air.

## Final list (accepted)
**Creatures (10):** 4 Murmuring Mystic, 3 Thorn of the Black Rose, 1 Troll of Khazad-dûm, 1 Gurmag Angler, 1 Mystical Teachings (an instant, listed here for the count)
**Card selection and draw (13):** 4 Brainstorm, 3 Preordain, 2 Ponder, 2 Deep Analysis, 2 Deduce, 2 Think Twice
**Interaction (17):** 4 Counterspell, 2 Prohibit, 1 Exclude, 3 Cast Down, 2 Snuff Out, 2 Agony Warp, 2 Suffocating Fumes
**Lands (19):** 4 Contaminated Aquifer, 2 Dimir Aqueduct, 2 Seething Landscape, 1 Bojuka Bog, 5 Island, 5 Swamp

**Sideboard (15):** 4 Hydroblast, 2 Blue Elemental Blast, 2 Annul, 1 Steel Sabotage, 2 Relic of Progenitus, 2 Arms of Hadar, 2 Duress

## What I changed from the submitted deck
The top of the current meta is Madness 16.4%, Terror 12.8%, Tron 10.3% and Faeries 8.2%. Madness, the biggest deck, is the one this list fears most.
- **Removed 1 Dimir Aqueduct, added 1 Swamp.** The deck had 8 lands that enter tapped, which is too many against Madness's burn. It now has 7.
- **Removed 1 Exclude, added a second Agony Warp.** Agony Warp costs 2 instead of 3, and it shrinks one attacker and weakens another. That suits a deck under early pressure better than a 3-mana counter that only hits creatures.
- **Sideboard: removed 1 Annul, added 1 Steel Sabotage.** It can bounce an artifact that's already in play, not just counter one, which matters against Affinity (3.7%).
- **Tried and dropped:** I wanted Lórien Revealed instead of Deduce. It's the most-played draw spell among blue decks here (24.6% of lists), and it can be cycled for 1 mana to fetch an Island or Contaminated Aquifer. The submit check rejected that version (and one with Dispel) because the main deck matched an existing UW Control list too closely (66.7%, then 61.7%, against a 60% limit). So it stays with Deduce.

## Why the key cards
- **Murmuring Mystic** has 1/5 stats, so Lightning Bolt doesn't kill it, and 20 of your 41 non-land cards are instants or sorceries that make birds.
- **Thorn of the Black Rose** gives you the monarch, and its deathtouch body scares off ground attackers.
- **Think Twice and Deep Analysis** can be cast a second time from the graveyard (flashback), so each one makes two birds.
- **Mystical Teachings** fetches whatever instant you need.
- **Troll of Khazad-dûm** can be cycled for 1 mana to find a Swamp early, or cast as a big threat late.
- **Contaminated Aquifer** has the Island and Swamp types, so you always control a Swamp for Snuff Out's free mode (pay 4 life instead of mana).

## The mana (simulated over 5,000 games, no mulligans assumed beyond the sim's own)
- 19 lands. The deck check recommends about 16.8, and Faeries lists run about 18.1.
- Mulligan rate 8.4%. Screw rate 29.4%, compared with 32.8% for a real Faeries list.
- Having the right colors rises from 80.2% on turn 3 to 85.8% on turn 5. That's a bit lower than the earlier split I tried (6 Island/4 Swamp, 88.2% on turn 5), because the deck leans blue.
- **The honest number:** you have Mystic or Thorn in hand by turn 5 in 56.8% of games, but have it *in hand and castable* in only 24.6%. The simulator doesn't count Brainstorm, Ponder or Troll's land-cycling, so the real rate should be somewhat higher (my judgment). This is a slow deck, and the payoffs will often come down on turn 5–6.

## Sideboarding (my judgment, not tested in matches)
- **Madness (worst common matchup):** bring in 4 Hydroblast and 2 Blue Elemental Blast (they counter Lightning Bolt and Fireblast, or destroy Guttersnipe). Take out Exclude, Mystical Teachings, Gurmag Angler and some of the 2 Deduce / 2 Think Twice. Watch your life: Snuff Out's free mode costs 4 and Deep Analysis's flashback costs 3. Don't make yourself monarch before you can defend it.
- **Terror and Faeries:** bring in the Blasts (both decks are blue), plus Arms of Hadar against Faeries' small fliers. Take out Exclude and the Suffocating Fumes.
- **Tron:** bring in 2 Duress, 2 Annul and Relic of Progenitus. Take out Cast Down, Agony Warp and Suffocating Fumes. Save Counterspell for their big spells, not their land-searching ones.
- **Elves and Mono-Red Rally:** bring in Arms of Hadar. It's a sorcery, so it also makes a bird.
- **Affinity:** bring in Annul, Steel Sabotage and the Blasts (for red artifacts).

## Label and what's unverified
This is a **brew**. The lands copy Faeries' setup (Contaminated Aquifer, Seething Landscape, Bojuka Bog, Dimir Aqueduct), and the sideboard follows what Faeries and Terror players run. Every card is confirmed Pauper-legal. Nothing here has been tested in real matches:
- Which matchups the deck is good or bad in is my judgment from the meta, not results.
- Deduce and Think Twice have almost no tournament history (3 and 0 lists in the last 90 days).
- Sweepers and damage-to-everything effects will wipe out your birds.

# Mono-Blue Medallion Freeze (Premodern brew)

## The plan
Get Sapphire Medallion and/or Helm of Awakening onto the table on turns 2–3. Once both are out, Cloud of Faeries, Snap and Merchant Scroll cost {U}, and Frantic Search and Brain Freeze cost {U} or nothing. Then take one big turn: each untap spell gives back more mana than it costs, and every spell adds to the storm count. Finish with one or more Brain Freezes. Each copy mills 3 cards, so a full library needs about 16+ copies, spread across one or more Freezes.

## Decklist (submitted and accepted)
**Main (60)**
- 4 Sapphire Medallion
- 4 Helm of Awakening
- 4 Brain Freeze
- 4 Cloud of Faeries
- 4 Snap
- 4 Frantic Search
- 4 Merchant Scroll
- 4 Gush
- 2 Turnabout
- 2 Peregrine Drake
- 2 Lotus Petal
- 1 Opt
- 21 Island

**Sideboard (15)**
- 3 Hydroblast
- 3 Counterspell
- 2 Daze
- 2 Annul
- 2 Hibernation
- 2 Powder Keg
- 1 Chain of Vapor

## Why these cards
- **Cloud of Faeries + Snap:** Cloud untaps 2 lands when it enters, and Snap untaps 2 lands. Snap your own Cloud, recast it, and repeat. Each pass adds 2 to the storm count and gives back mana.
- **Peregrine Drake:** it untaps up to five lands. With both reducers it costs {2}{U}, so Snapping it back and recasting it is the biggest mana loop in the deck. (That loop is my own math.)
- **Frantic Search:** untaps 3 lands and filters your draws.
- **Turnabout:** untaps every land you control.
- **Gush:** you can cast it for free by returning two Islands to your hand. That's a spell for storm count plus two cards, and it doesn't cost your mana.
- **Merchant Scroll:** finds Brain Freeze, or whatever instant is missing (Snap, Frantic Search, Turnabout or Gush).
- **Helm of Awakening is a real downside:** it makes the opponent's spells cheaper too. Against creature decks, try to win with Medallion and the untappers, and only play Helm on the turn you go off.

## The mana (5,000 simulated games, no card abilities modeled)
- The deck mulligans 8.7% of the time.
- It has its fourth land by turn 4 in 49.8% of games and counts as screwed in 20.4%. Flood is 0.7%.
- By turn 5, a reducer, a Brain Freeze or Merchant Scroll, and an untapper are all in hand and castable 62.5% of the time.
- **I tested 22 Islands with no Opt:** screw fell to 10.2%, but mulligans rose to 20.1% and the turn-5 engine rate fell to 60.6%. I kept 21. If you keep getting stuck on lands, the 22nd Island is the swap to make.
- The simulator doesn't play out the combo itself, so I haven't measured how often you actually win. That depends on how you sequence the turn.

## The field and sideboarding
The current meta: Sligh 12.8%, Stiflenought 11%, Elves 10.4%, Goblins 9.1%, Oath Ponza 6.1%, Enchantress 5.5%.

- **Sligh / Goblins (worst matchups, about 22% combined):** bring in 3 Hydroblast and 2 Powder Keg. Keg with one counter kills their 1-drops. Take out 2 Helm and 2 Gush (Gush sets back your land drops when you need to race). Don't play Helm early.
- **Stiflenought (Counterspell, Daze, Stifle and Annul in nearly every list):** bring in 3 Counterspell, 2 Daze and 1 Hydroblast. Take out 2 Peregrine Drake and 2–3 Helm. Annul hits your artifacts and Stifle can counter a storm trigger, so make them use their counters before you cast Freeze, or Freeze twice.
- **Elves:** bring in 2 Hibernation and 2 Powder Keg. Hibernation costs {U} with both reducers out and resets their whole board. Take out 2 Helm (it speeds them up) and 2 Gush.
  - Gaea's Blessing (it shuffles their graveyard back when milled) shows up in 5 of 17 Elves mains and in about 29% of their sideboards. It's also in 5 Enchantress lists.
  - Against Blessing, mill in one big turn. Another option, which I haven't tested: Merchant Scroll for Brain Freeze, plus enough copies to mill past it.
  - Chain of Vapor comes in against Tangle Wire, which about half of Elves lists play.
- **Control, Stasis, Oath and Enchantress:** these are your best matchups. Bring in 2 Counterspell and 2 Annul (Annul counters Oath of Druids and Stasis). Take out 2 Peregrine Drake and 1 Opt or 1 Gush.

## What changed from the submitted version
The main deck is unchanged. In the sideboard I cut 2 Blue Elemental Blast (it duplicates Hydroblast), 1 Daze and 1 Chain of Vapor. In their place I added 2 Hibernation and 2 Powder Keg. Elves made up 10.4% of the field and the old sideboard had nothing for it. Keg also helps against Goblins.

## Label and what's unverified
- **Label:** this is a brew. Its mono-blue mana and counter suite come from Stiflenought, which plays 16 Islands on average plus Gush, Daze and Counterspell. In the last 90 days, Medallion, Helm, Merchant Scroll, Turnabout and Peregrine Drake appeared in 0 results, so this exact deck hasn't been proven in tournaments.
- **Unverified:**
  - The "16+ copies by turn 5" target is an estimate.
  - The matchup claims are my judgment from what the top decks play, not measured win rates.

There's a "Mono-Red Land Destruction" strategy in the results. Let me pull it.

I built you a mono-red prison deck. No "Mono Red Prison" or "Ponza" archetype shows up under those names in the last 30 days of Premodern results, but the card data shows a **Mono-Red Land Destruction** archetype that does exactly what you asked for. I used its latest top list without changes, a 5-0 Premodern League finish from 2026-10-01. It's a small archetype, with only 7 lists in the data, and it isn't one of the 20 biggest strategies in the meta.

**The plan**
Destroy or tap down the opponent's lands so they can't cast spells, and punish the cards stuck in their hand with Black Vise. Burn handles their creatures, and cheap threats and creature lands (Mishra's Factory, Ghitu Encampment, Barbarian Ring) finish the game. All your bounce-back comes from Mountains and colorless lands, while they're stuck on one or two lands.

**Main deck (60)**
- 4 Stone Rain, 3 Pillage, 4 Avalanche Riders, 1 Dwarven Miner
- 3 Black Vise, 1 Cursed Scroll, 2 Phyrexian Furnace
- 4 Mogg Fanatic, 2 Grim Lavamancer
- 4 Lightning Bolt, 2 Incinerate, 2 Firebolt, 2 Earthquake
- 11 Mountain, 4 Wasteland, 4 Rishadan Port, 4 Mishra's Factory, 2 Ghitu Encampment, 1 Barbarian Ring

**Sideboard (15)**
- 4 Overload, 4 Red Elemental Blast, 2 Pyroblast, 2 Anarchy, 2 Aftershock, 1 Tormod's Crypt

**Why these cards**
- **Stone Rain and Pillage:** your main 3-mana land destruction. Pillage ("destroy target artifact or land") can also hit artifacts.
- **Avalanche Riders:** has haste and destroys a land when it enters, so it attacks and destroys a land the same turn.
- **Wasteland, Rishadan Port and Dwarven Miner:** they destroy or tap lands from your land slots, so the lock starts on turns 1–2.
- **Black Vise:** deals damage each upkeep equal to the cards in their hand minus 4. That's the payoff for keeping them from casting their spells.
- **Burn, Mogg Fanatic and Lavamancer:** they clear early creatures so the lock doesn't get attacked down.
- **Phyrexian Furnace:** graveyard hate that also draws a card.

**Mana (5,000 simulated games)**
- **Lands:** 26, matching the real lists (average 26.3). Average mana value of the spells is 1.85.
- **Red sources:** 14.
- **Mulligans and land drops:** 12.8% of hands mulligan. You make every land drop through turn 4 in 77.3% of games; mana screw is 5.3% and flood is 5.9%. You have about 2.9 lands in play on turn 3.
- **Red mana:** you have the red you need 80.8% of the time on turn 3, and 86–92% from turn 4 on. The dip comes from 12 colorless lands (Port, Wasteland, Factory). Lead with Mountains when you have a choice.
- **Draw odds (on the play):** 70% to have Stone Rain or Pillage by turn 3. 97.6% to have some land-attack card by turn 3 (any of the 19 Stone Rains, Pillages, Wastelands, Ports or Riders). Riders cost 4, so they're usually a turn-4 play.

**Sideboarding against the current top decks** (meta shares are measured; the swaps are my judgment)
- **Enchantress (12.5%) and Terrageddon (11.2%):** bring in Anarchy, which destroys all white permanents, plus Overload and Aftershock for key artifacts. Your Wastelands and Ports are good here.
- **Stiflenought (10.4%) and UB Psychatog (4.8%):** bring in Red Elemental Blast and Pyroblast against their blue spells, and Overload for small artifacts. Take out Black Vise against Stiflenought and Earthquake against Psychatog.
- **Sligh (9.9%) and Goblins (4.4%):** Black Vise is weak because they empty their hands quickly, so cut it. Keep all the burn and Earthquake, and add Overload for their cheap artifacts.
- **Hermit Druid Combo (5.5%) and Replenish (4.8%):** bring in Tormod's Crypt and keep both Furnaces. Land destruction is your main way to slow them down.

**Label:** stock. It's the Mono-Red Land Destruction reference list unchanged, and it passed the deck check with no errors or warnings.

**Not verified**
- The deck is legal and its mana matches the real lists, but 7 lists is a small sample. I can't tell you how well it does against the field, because no tool measured win rates.
- I didn't look up Pyroblast's card text or the mana values of the opponents' key artifacts (for example, Stiflenought's Phyrexian Dreadnought). Whether unkicked Overload kills Dreadnought is my assumption, not checked.

results.text:
**Bazaar Dredge (stock), Vintage**

**Why this deck.** Most of the top Vintage decks right now run Power Nine. The two biggest non-Lurrus decks, Mono-White Initiative (12.1% of the field) and Raker Shops (9.1%), both play it: the latest 5-0 Initiative list has Black Lotus and all five Moxen. I only pulled the Initiative list myself; the Shops claim is my judgment. Dredge is the most-played deck in the last 30 days that doesn't need Power: 26 lists, 3.9% of the field. In the 94 Dredge lists recorded, Moxen and Lotus each show up in only 2–3%. The other Power-free Bazaar deck, Hollow Vine, is smaller (1.6%). That makes Dredge the safest answer to "most competitive without Power." That's based on how many people play it; no tool measured win rates.

**The list** (Vintage Challenge, 8th place, 4-3, 2026-10-11)
- **Lands (4):** 4 Bazaar of Baghdad
- **Creatures (37):** 4 Golgari Thug, 4 Stinkweed Imp, 1 Golgari Grave-Troll, 4 Ichorid, 4 Narcomoeba, 4 Prized Amalgam, 4 Shambling Shell, 4 Silversmote Ghoul, 4 Hollow One, 4 Grief
- **Spells (19):** 4 Creeping Chill, 4 Noxious Revival, 4 Force of Will, 1 Force of Negation, 1 Mental Misstep, 1 Chalice of the Void, 4 Serum Powder
- **Sideboard (15):** 4 Force of Vigor, 4 Sickening Shoal, 3 Force of Negation, 3 Wasteland, 1 Strip Mine

**The plan.** Bazaar draws two and discards three each turn. Instead of drawing normally, you dredge the cards with dredge (Thug, Imp, Grave-Troll) to fill your graveyard quickly.
- Narcomoeba comes into play free when milled.
- Each Creeping Chill that gets milled deals 3 damage and gains you 3 life. That life gain brings back Silversmote Ghoul.
- Ichorid returns from the graveyard every upkeep, and Prized Amalgam returns at the end of the turn.
- Hollow One costs nothing after one Bazaar activation (each discarded card makes it 2 cheaper).
- The deck needs almost no mana. Grief, Force of Will and Force of Negation can all be cast free, which lets you strip a key card or counter one on turn 1.

**Mana and consistency**
- **Odds of a Bazaar:** 39.9% in your opening 7 on the play and 44.5% by your first draw on the draw (exact odds, measured). That's why the deck runs 4 Serum Powder: it lets you swap your whole hand for a new one before deciding to mulligan.
- **The simulation doesn't fit this deck.** It reported a 60.2% mulligan rate and 98.4% "mana screw," because it treats 4 lands as a broken mana base and can't use Serum Powder. In practice, Dredge players do mulligan hard to find Bazaar, so the high mulligan rate is roughly real. The screw number isn't: the deck barely uses mana.
- **Deck check:** passed with no issues. 4 lands sits within the normal Dredge range (average 4.57).

**Sideboarding** (which cards go in is from the stock list; the matchup advice is my judgment)
- **Against graveyard hate** (Leyline of the Void, Rest in Peace, both in the Initiative sideboard) **and against Shops:** bring in Force of Vigor. It's free on their turn and destroys two artifacts or enchantments.
- **Against Initiative and creature decks** (White Plume Adventurer, Archon of Emeria, Witch Enchanter): bring in Sickening Shoal as free removal.
- **Against combo** (Paradoxical Outcome, Tinker, Oath, Underworld Breach, Doomsday): bring in the 3 extra Force of Negation.
- **Against Shops and Initiative:** Wasteland and Strip Mine can hit Ancient Tomb, Karakas and Cavern of Souls.
- Cut cards like Chalice, Mental Misstep or some Hollow Ones depending on the matchup.

**Label:** stock. This is the most recent top-finishing Dredge list, unchanged.

**Not verified**
- It's a 4-3 Top 8 finish, not a tournament win.
- No tool measured how this deck does against specific opponents. The matchup notes above are my judgment.

results.prompt: Mono black tron in Modern?
results.text:
I reviewed this against the current Modern field and made one revision: two Eldrazi Temple and a sharper sideboard. The black cards and Tron payoffs stayed locked.

## The plan
This is mono-black Tron. You put the Urza lands together with Expedition Map, Urza's Cave and cheap artifacts. Then you cast Karn, the Great Creator and Thought-Knot Seer turns early, and finish with Wurmcoil Engine, Ulamog or All Is Dust. Black doesn't get Ancient Stirrings, so the deck isn't built to need Tron. Every 4-drop works off any four lands, and Fatal Push, Thoughtseize and Kozilek's Command buy time until then.

## Why the key cards
- **Karn, the Great Creator:** turns off activated abilities of your opponent's artifacts. That stops Affinity and also stops Broodscale Combo from equipping Blade of the Bloodchief. Its −2 lets you fetch an artifact from your sideboard, so 11 of the sideboard cards are artifacts you can grab mid-game.
- **Thought-Knot Seer and Thoughtseize:** strip combo pieces and answers out of the opponent's hand.
- **Fatal Push:** Expedition Map, Chromatic Star, Mind Stone, Urza's Cave, Deadly Dispute and Wurmcoil all make it easy to turn on revolt, which raises Push's reach from 2-mana creatures to 4-mana ones.
- **New: Eldrazi Temple (2 copies).** It's colorless, so it fits mono-black, and it's in all 412 recent Eldrazi Tron lists. Its two-mana mode pays for Thought-Knot Seer, Kozilek's Command, Ulamog and All Is Dust, which are all colorless Eldrazi.

## Mana (5,000 simulated games each)
| | Submitted (23 lands, 4 Mind Stone) | **Final (25 lands, 2 Mind Stone)** | Real Eldrazi Tron list |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mulligan rate | 17.5% | **14.2%** | 18.0% |
| Too few lands (screw) | 9.3% | **6.2%** | 8.9% |
| Too many lands (flood) | 2.7% | 4.7% | 2.7% |
| Karn or Thought-Knot Seer castable by turn 4 | 61.1% | **65.7%** | — |
| Black mana on turn 1 | 90.7% | 90.1% | — |

- I tested a 24-land version too (7 Swamp, 3 Mind Stone). It came out worse: 63.7% castable by turn 4, and black on turn 1 fell to 88.7%.
- The deck checker points out that real Eldrazi Tron lists run about 22.3 lands. I kept the extra lands because this deck has no Ancient Stirrings to find them. The cost is flood going up 2 points.
- Black sources are 8 Swamp, Urborg, Chromatic Star and the Treasure from Deadly Dispute.

## Matchups and sideboarding
These shares come from the last 30 days of results.

- **Broodscale Combo (14.4%), your worst matchup.** It's the most played deck and it's fast.
  - In: Cursed Totem, Disruptor Flute (name Basking Broodscale), Trinisphere, 4th Thoughtseize.
  - Out: 2 Wurmcoil, All Is Dust, 1 Kozilek's Command.
  - Cursed Totem stops all activated abilities of creatures, so it shuts off Broodscale's Adapt and the Spawn tokens' "sacrifice: add mana."
  - All Is Dust only removes colored permanents, and Broodscale is colorless, so it misses.
  - They run Haywire Mite and Nature's Claim, so your artifacts can be destroyed.
- **Prowess (9.9%).**
  - In: 2 Toxic Deluge, plus Ensnaring Bridge and Walking Ballista (or fetch them with Karn).
  - Out: 2 Ulamog, some Thoughtseize (it costs you life you can't spare).
- **Devoted Druid Combo (5.1%):** Cursed Totem, Ballista and Disruptor Flute. Fatal Push is already in the main deck.
- **Storm and Goryo's Vengeance (3.7% each), Living End (2.4%):**
  - In: Thoughtseize, Trinisphere against Storm.
  - In: Tormod's Crypt, Grafdigger's Cage and the new Bojuka Bog against the graveyard decks.
  - Out: Wurmcoil, All Is Dust.
- **Affinity, Energy and Domain Zoo:** Karn and Wurmcoil do the work. Add Toxic Deluge against creature swarms.
- **UW and Jeskai Control:** cut some Fatal Push, add the 4th Thoughtseize, and use Karn to fetch The Stone Brain.
- **Boros Land Destruction (1.8%):** this will stay a bad matchup. Expedition Map and Urza's Cave help you rebuild.

To make room in the sideboard I cut Dismember and Sheoldred's Edict, since 4 Fatal Push already handle small creatures. Disruptor Flute and Bojuka Bog took their places.

## Label and what's unverified
**Brew.** The Tron lands, Karn and the sideboard artifacts come from Eldrazi Tron. The all-black shell is new.
- Wurmcoil Engine showed up in just 1 Modern list in the last 90 days, Chromatic Star in 2 and Deadly Dispute in 0. Those slots are my judgment, not proven choices.
- The simulator only counts how much mana a land produces, so it doesn't model Temple's Eldrazi-only two-mana mode. Temple's real value for Thought-Knot Seer is probably higher than the table shows.
- I didn't measure any matchup win rates. The matchup read above is based on what each card does.

results.prompt: City of Traitors mono black premodern deck?
results.text:
# Mono-Black City of Traitors: fast mana into big threats (Premodern brew)

**The plan:** City of Traitors, Ancient Tomb and Dark Ritual let you cast 3–4 mana threats on turn 1 or 2. Those are Hypnotic Specter, Phyrexian Negator, Masticore, Phyrexian Scuta, Phyrexian Processor and Tangle Wire. Duress and Cabal Therapy clear counterspells and answers out of the opponent's hand first. City is a one-shot burst of mana: you're happy to lose it once your threat is down. When the opponent is short on lands, Tangle Wire can keep them stuck while your creatures attack.

## Main deck (60)
**Lands (23):** 4 City of Traitors, 4 Ancient Tomb, 14 Swamp, 1 Cabal Pit
**Fast mana (4):** 4 Dark Ritual
**Threats (18):** 4 Hypnotic Specter, 4 Phyrexian Negator, 3 Masticore, 2 Phyrexian Scuta, 2 Phyrexian Processor, 3 Tangle Wire
**Discard (6):** 4 Duress, 2 Cabal Therapy
**Removal (5):** 2 Smother, 2 Diabolic Edict, 1 Snuff Out
**Other (4):** 2 Cursed Scroll, 2 Bottle Gnomes

## Sideboard (15)
3 Engineered Plague, 3 Dystopia, 2 Gloom, 2 Tormod's Crypt, 2 Powder Keg, 2 Vendetta, 1 Drain Life

## Why these cards
- **City of Traitors and Ancient Tomb** each tap for two colorless mana. With a Swamp or Dark Ritual, that's enough for Negator (2B), Masticore (4), Tangle Wire (3) or Processor (4) on turn 1 or 2.
- **Specter and Negator** are the fastest real clocks. Negator is a 5/5 trampler for 3, but you sacrifice a permanent for each point of damage dealt to it.
- **Masticore** answers creature decks by itself (it pings for 2 mana and regenerates).
- **Tangle Wire** hurts the opponent more than you, because your burst mana has already been spent.

## What I changed from the submitted deck
The core cards weren't touched; only these slots changed.
- **2 Chimeric Idol → 2 Bottle Gnomes.** Idol taps all your lands, which fights with the mana you need for Masticore and Processor. Gnomes cost 3 colorless, so Tomb or City casts them. They gain 3 life against burn, and they're spare creatures to tap for Tangle Wire or sacrifice to flash back Cabal Therapy.
- **1 Cabal Pit → 1 Swamp.** That's one less land that costs you life, and one less nonbasic for Price of Progress, which 34% of Sligh lists run. You keep the same 15 black sources.
- **Sideboard: 1 Ravenous Rats → 1 Drain Life,** for life gain against burn.
- **Not kept:** I tried 2 Withered Wretch and later 2 Ravenous Rats in the Gnomes slots.
  - Wretch costs BB, and the simulation showed it dropped your chance of having the right colors on turn 2 from 96.3% to 83.4%.
  - Rats pushed the deck too close to an existing Moneyball Black list for it to count as a brew.

## The mana (5,000 simulated games)
- **Mulligans:** 17.5%, against 8.6% for a current Moneyball Black list. This is the real cost of 8 colorless lands plus Specter's BB.
- **Running short on lands:** 9.3% screw (vs 21.5% for Moneyball) and 67% of games hit every land drop through turn 4 (vs 50%).
- **Right colors in play:** 95.7% on turn 1, 96.3% on turn 2, but only 87.6% on turn 3. A Tomb-or-City hand that needs BB for Specter is the usual stumble.
- **Fast start:** A turn-2 threat is in your hand 77.4% of the time. The simulation doesn't count Dark Ritual, so I can't give you a measured number for actually casting it on turn 2.
- **Land count:** 23, with 15 black sources. That matches the Moneyball Black average of 23.15 lands, though those lists run about 17.3 black sources.

## Sideboarding against the field (last 30 days)
- **Enchantress (12.5%):** Bring in 3 Dystopia and 2 Gloom; take out 2 Smother, 2 Diabolic Edict and 1 Snuff Out (they have almost no creatures to target). Keep all the discard. Expect Swords to Plowshares on your threats.
- **Terrageddon (11.2%):** Bring in Dystopia and 1–2 Engineered Plague. Their 4 Wasteland and Armageddon punish keeping City around, so cast your threat right away. Masticore and the Edicts handle Terravore and the Mongooses.
- **Stiflenought (10.4%):** Take out 2 Bottle Gnomes and 1 Smother. Discard and Edict/Snuff Out handle Phyrexian Dreadnought (Snuff Out works because it's a nonblack artifact creature). Watch for their Powder Keg; it sweeps your 3-drops at three counters.
- **Sligh (9.9%) and Goblins (4.4%), your worst matchups:**
  - Bring in 2 Vendetta (kills Grim Lavamancer and Goblins for 1 life), Drain Life and Engineered Plague (vs Goblins), plus Powder Keg (vs Goblins).
  - Take out Phyrexian Processor, Scuta and Cabal Therapy.
  - Burn kills Specter easily, and Negator's sacrifice drawback hurts. Fetch and mana-land Tomb damage carefully.
- **Hermit Druid (5.5%) and Replenish (4.8%):** Bring in 2 Tormod's Crypt. Keep all the discard and take out removal.

## Label and what's unverified
- **Label:** This is a **brew**. It borrows its removal suite, Cursed Scroll and sideboard from Moneyball Black, and the City/Tomb/Tangle Wire/Processor package is new.
- **Unverified:** The matchup judgments above are my reasoning from the decks' card lists, not tested results. Phyrexian Processor, Scuta and Tangle Wire barely show up in recent tournament results, so they're untested in this shell.

results.prompt: Best 5 color Solution deck in premodern?
results.text:
I didn't find a deck called "Solution" in the Premodern results. A search under "Solution", "The Solution", "5 Color Solution", "5C", "Domain" and "Five Color" turned up nothing. So I've assumed you mean the most-played true five-color deck in the current results, **Hermit Druid Combo** (a Survival of the Fittest graveyard-combo deck). It makes up 5.5% of the field, with 42 lists in the last 30 days. The base is its most recent top list, a 5-0 Premodern League finish (2026-10-13), and I haven't changed it.

**The plan**
Make mana with Birds, Wall of Roots and Elvish Spirit Guide, then land a Hermit Druid or a Survival of the Fittest by turn 2–3. With 22 lands and none of them basic, an active Hermit Druid should mill most or all of your library. Then a reanimation spell (Unearth, Animate Dead, Shallow Grave) or the Volrath's Shapeshifter / Krosan Reclamation package turns that graveyard into a win. Survival is the second way in: it lets you discard the right creatures and set up the same finish without Druid.

**Why the key cards**
- **4 Hermit Druid, 4 Survival of the Fittest:** the two engines. All 93 lists in the archetype data run 4 Druid, and the lists that play Survival run 4.
- **The single-copy creatures** (Akroma, Karmic Guide, Palinchron, Phyrexian Devourer, Psychatog, Squee, Triskelion, Battlefield Scrounger, plus 2 Shapeshifter) are the combo pieces and finishers. Each one appears in about 86–87% of lists.
- **4 Cabal Therapy:** protects the combo by stripping counterspells and hate cards. It's in 100% of lists.
- I haven't checked these cards' exact rules text this session. The combo lines above are the usual way the deck plays, not something I traced step by step. Read the cards before you sleeve up.

**Mana (measured)**
- 22 lands, 2.53 average mana value. Colored sources: G 24, U 19, B 18, W 16, R 14, all within the normal range for this archetype (for example, 23.2 G and 19.5 U on average). check_deck found no issues.
- Over 5,000 simulated games: 19.7% mulligan rate, 10.4% mana screw, 1.9% flood.
- Correct colors: 86.1% on turn 1, 98.5% on turn 2.
- Hermit Druid or Survival in hand and castable by turn 2: 41.1%. This doesn't count digging or mulligans.
- The mulligan rate is high because the deck keeps only hands that can find its engine.

**Sideboarding (judgment, based on the field)**
- **Sligh, Goblins, GR Zoo (fast red decks):** bring in Pyroclasm ×2, plus Swords to Plowshares if your build has room. Cut slow pieces like Shallow Grave.
- **Stiflenought, UB Psychatog, Standstill (blue tempo and counterspells):** bring in Xantid Swarm ×2 and Duress ×2, and keep all four Therapy.
- **Enchantress, Replenish (enchantment decks):** bring in Naturalize ×2, Ray of Revelation, Monk Realist and Uktabi Orangutan. Enlightened Tutor finds the answer you need.
- **Terrageddon (land destruction):** Elvish Spirit Guide and the mana creatures carry you through. Swords handles their threats.
- **Graveyard hate in general:** the Survival line and Unearth help you rebuild. Eladamri's Vineyard and Ghitu Slinger are niche cards that the list carries.

**Status:** stock, the latest 5-0 Hermit Druid Combo list, unchanged. The deck passed the legality and color checks. Unverified: whether this is the deck you call "Solution". If that name refers to a different five-color build (for example, an old-school control deck), tell me and I'll rebuild around it, keeping in mind it has no recent results to work from.
